newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas firms in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas firms in active trade.

text.p: Gasoline firmed in an active market amid improving fundamentals, traders said on Monday.

After a quiet week on the fob Singapore market last week, 50,00-barrels of unleaded 97-octane lifting June 12-16 traded at $25.50 per barrel, 100,000-barrels of 95-octane at $24.25 for June 10-12 and 50,000-barrels of 92-octane at $23.50 for June 10-14.
Traders said the length in the market should ease as the region heads into the summer driving season with exports from China and South Korea absorbed by strong domestic demand.
India's tender to buy 25,000-tonnes for June 10-14 delivery to Bombay, closing Wednesday, will also remove some of the length, they said.
Naphtha was comparatively quieter although June swaps quoted at $22.40/$22.60 per barrel, was 15-20 cents firmer from Friday.
The Petrochemical Corporation of Singapore (PCS) which started up its number one ethylene plant over the weekend, is expected to reach full production soon, a company official said.
A source close to the company told Reuters the plant was already on-spec.

The 450,000-tonne-per-year plant was shut down on a week ago for government officials to carry out investigations following the death of two divers while clearing debris at the unit's seawater intake pit.
